title: DICTO: Collected Geometric Works
description:
DICTO is a geometric sculptor in Osaka. The work grows out of building with recycled PET bottles and from three open apps on one shared geometry: Kaleidohedra, Rhombiverse and Polyhedraverse.

This record gathers all of DICTO's published geometry in one place. It opens with a short essay, Quanta of Space, which reads the works as a study of the pieces from which space is built, from the atoms of the ancients (Democritus, Plato's Timaeus) to the quanta of modern physics (loop quantum gravity), and as a bridge between periodic and aperiodic order. The papers follow in four chapters: Atoms (new solids), Bonds (how pieces fill space), Shells (layers round a core) and Cycles (rules that turn one shell into the next). Each paper has its own DICTO DOI, which always opens its newest version; the numbers (#1, #2 …) are the paper numbers on dictospheres.com; DICTO's findings are numbered separately, F1, F2 ….

Version 30 (27 October 2026) adds #58, From the Octet to Every Stacking: the Web of Bonds, and #59, The Icosaxes Hexa: Bloom, Bud and Seed. Version 28 (25 October 2026) adds #56, Sonsam and Lahdeli: the Delian Bond on the Twinned Octet, with Ian Dury, Blockhead and Keyed Switch Points, and lists the solids named in the Bonds papers under Atoms. Version 27 (25 October 2026) adds #54, One Turn Is a Gnomon: the Golden Cycle Step by Step, and the Polar of the Keyed Pair. Version 26 (25 October 2026) adds #55, David and Goliath: Jessen's Icosahedron and the Tetrahedron in the A15 Weight Walk. Version 25 (25 October 2026) adds #53, The Global Web of Bonds: How Bonds Hand Over Across Crystal Networks. Version 24 (25 October 2026) adds #52, The Web of Bonds: How the DICTONIC Bonds Hand Over; lists the newest papers first, with a What's new box on the first page; names the six DICTONIC SOLIDS and three DICTONIC BONDS in the introduction; and lists the DICTONIC world and the data set DICTO Solids: Exact Geometry (DICTO DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23606967). Version 23 (24 October 2026) added #50, One Move Each.

Findings and apps: Kaleidohedra by DICTO, DICTO DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23173809: DICTO's findings with the open apps' code. Findings published there without a separate paper: F1 DICTO skewed rhombic dodecahedron; F5 Regular-hexagon elongated dodecahedron (found independently; known, Grünbaum 2010); F10 DICTO Jewel (EKP windows); F11 The stretched dodecahedron; F12 Star Chain Reaction; F15 DICTO Jewel clusters; F16 Sunstar clusters.
